title: Your First 30 Days at Work
summary: Create a practical first-30-days plan for learning expectations, building reliable habits, receiving feedback, and succeeding in a new workplace.
objectives: Identify priorities for the first days and weeks of a new job.
Plan how to learn procedures, ask questions, organize information, and use feedback.
Create an actionable First-30-Days Workplace Plan.

vocab.def: The process of helping a new worker understand the organization, role, policies, tools, people, and expectations.
An established sequence or method for completing a task or process.
A planned conversation used to review progress, questions, expectations, or support needs.
A documented set of specific steps used to reach a goal.

sections.heading: Your first job is to learn the environment
sections.body: During the first days of work, pay attention to role expectations, schedule requirements, safety rules, communication channels, supervision, workplace culture, accessibility or accommodation processes, and how work is assigned and reviewed.

sections.heading: Ask useful questions
sections.body: Good questions are specific and show what you already understand. Before asking, identify what is unclear. When appropriate, take notes so that the same information does not need to be repeatedly explained.

sections.heading: Use feedback as information
sections.body: Feedback can help you adjust before small misunderstandings become repeated problems. Listen carefully, ask for examples when needed, identify what should change, and apply the correction to future work.

sections.heading: Build relationships through dependable behavior
sections.body: Trust usually develops through repeated behavior: arriving prepared, communicating accurately, completing commitments, treating people respectfully, protecting information, asking for help when appropriate, and showing that feedback leads to improvement.

sections.heading: Make the first month intentional
sections.body: A First-30-Days Workplace Plan can organize what you need to learn, who can answer different questions, what procedures matter most, how you will track responsibilities, what feedback you need, and what habits will support reliability.

practice.prompt: You have received several new procedures during your first week and are having trouble remembering the sequence. What is a productive response?
practice.answer: Use approved notes or reference materials, identify the part that is unclear, and ask an appropriate person to confirm the procedure.

practice.prompt: Your supervisor gives feedback about something you should change. What should your plan include?
practice.answer: The specific change, how you will apply it, and a way to confirm later that your performance now matches the expectation.

quiz.question: What is the strongest purpose of a First-30-Days Workplace Plan?
options: Turn expectations, learning needs, communication, and reliability habits into specific actions
quiz.answer: Turn expectations, learning needs, communication, and reliability habits into specific actions

lab.objective: Create a First-30-Days Workplace Plan with learning priorities, reliability habits, questions, feedback checkpoints, communication expectations, and next actions.

reflectionPrompt: What is the most important habit you want to establish during your first month in a new workplace, and how will you know you are following it consistently?
